analyst_view.overall: Early view: two struggling sides. Slavia Prague are 34th with 1 point but pushed Arsenal late before losing 2-1, while Villarreal (28th, 3 points) were beaten 6-0 at home by PSG on matchday 4. The brief lists Santiago Mourino as banned after three yellow cards; he was booked against PSG but I could not confirm his earlier cautions. I found little fresh team news for either club, so this view rests on recent results and the table.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals and I lean lower. Slavia scored only once against Arsenal, late, and Villarreal's 6-0 defeat came against the best team in the competition. Both sides need to avoid losing ground, which may make this a more cautious game than the estimate suggests.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Slavia push hard at home, as they did late against Arsenal, while Villarreal should see more of the ball, which balances out. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and I lean slightly higher. Villarreal picked up three yellow cards even while losing 6-0 (Santi Comesana, Santiago Mourino, Sergi Cardona), and Slavia had David Moses booked against Arsenal. This is a must-win game for both, which tends to bring more fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.8 shots and I lean lower. Slavia's attack is limited (one goal against Arsenal), and Villarreal's confidence has taken a hit after the PSG defeat. I expect a total in the high twenties.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Neither side has looked sharp in front of goal recently in this competition, and I expect a tighter game than the numbers suggest.
